A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same study, The Importance of Being Lazy: Scaling Limits of Continual Learning. All 42 pages in each version are readable and comparable, including figures, equations, Table 1 and Appendices A–E.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural-network experiments and infinite-width simulations on CIFAR10, MNIST and TinyImagenet variants, with additional empirical analyses and synthetic-data validation in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and simulations, including the supplementary results in Appendices B, D and E.

M1.justification: The architectures, NTP and muP parameterizations, objectives and training procedures are unchanged. The edits to Proposition 4.1 concern its mathematical statement, without changing the method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same stationary and continual-learning datasets, task-similarity scenarios and synthetic Gaussian-data experiments. No dataset, domain or evaluated task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: NTP versus muP in Figure 2, and NTP, muP and muP+1/sqrt(L) in the depth experiments. No comparator membership changes.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendix A retain identical task splits, training budgets, model configurations and metrics, including the 30-sample MLP setup. The supplementary experimental protocols are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B retains the same training-duration, depth, feature-evolution, loss-landscape and CNN analyses. The simulation validation in Appendix D and synthetic analysis in Appendix E are likewise unchanged.

E5.justification: The five-seed averaging reported for Split-CIFAR10 and the feature-evolution/forgetting correlation significance in Section 5.1 remain unchanged. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Figures 1–25 retain the same plotted results, and the numerical and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout both versions. The corrected Figure 1 reference does not change any result.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.1 changes the variable named in its statement from gradient g^1 to pre-gradient z^1, matching Eq. (8). It also changes the Gaussian covariance from [K^x_{mu_i beta_j}] to [K^x_{mu_i}, K^x_{beta_j}] without defining the latter notation. These are localized formal revisions; the evolution equations and appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about parameterization-dependent forgetting, the lazy-rich transition and transfer of the optimal feature-learning level across widths.

C2.justification: The learning-rate explanation for the transition, the pretraining-effect interpretation and the stated limitations and future directions are unchanged. Correcting the figure reference in Section 5.1 does not revise its interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains identical architecture specifications, hyperparameters, initialization details, simulation procedures and hardware information. No implementation or code/data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Reference entries shift across page boundaries without changes to their content or the paper's relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: Local edits correct terminology in Proposition 4.1, remove an extra parenthesis in Eq. (5), add punctuation and change the Section 5.1 reference from Figure 1b to Figure 1c, which displays forgetting. The narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The revised proposition causes limited text reflow across columns and subsequent pages, including the references. All figures, Table 1, captions, axes and legends are retained; the appendix pages render identically.

improvement.justification: The pre-gradient correction, Eq. (5) cleanup and corrected Figure 1c reference improve local clarity. However, the revised covariance notation in Proposition 4.1 is unexplained and does not clearly express the joint covariance specified in unchanged Appendix C.2, Eqs. (49)–(52). With the empirical evidence and proofs otherwise unchanged, these benefits and the introduced mathematical ambiguity leave the net quality effect uncertain.
